findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Thermometer was not available in the meat freezer located in the back of the facility.  PIC was informed to provide a thermometer.  Ensure thermometers are present in cold holding units used for storage of TCS food.

4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
The floor drain for the three part sink in the back of the facility is observed to have a buildup of residue. An additional grate is also needed for the drain to prevent foreign objects from entering and potentially clogging the drain. Ensure the drain is properly cleaned as needed to prevent build-up. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Upon arrival, glass case holding cheeses, caviar, prosciutto, and butter observed holding ambient temperatures of 50 degrees in multiple places. Inspector checked temperatures of cheeses in various places in case and got a range of 45-50 temperatures. PIC noted the cooler was below 40 degrees upon her arrival at 8am this morning. No temperature logs are currently kept for this equipment. It is unknown how long the cooler had been sitting at temperatures of greater than 40 degrees. 

PIC contacted AirMasters to service cooler, will be able to service today within a few hours. PIC advised to retain an invoice from technician detailing services rendered and problems identified/fixed. 

The following items were voluntarily embargoed by PIC at time of inspection (permitted as well from owner via telephone): Belletoile cheese (x7), Petit Basque cheese (x2), Caviar (x11 cans), Creme fraiche (x7), Herb and garlic spreadable cheese (x5), Snofrisk cream cheese (x1 box), President French Butter (x2), Raclette cheese (x2), Port Salut cheese (x2). 

Owner requested permission to retain cheeses, caviar, and butter in the cooler until trash day next week so as not to create a nuisance (odor, pest, etc) in the back alley of facility. Inspector accepted this and consequently labeled each item with either an orange sticker with initials and date, or inspector initials in black sharpie to label the item not for sale, and to be discarded. Photographs of labeled items taken as well for added documentation. PIC instructed to ensure staff do not sell items bearing the sticker or inspector initials, that the items are to be discarded at next trash day. 

Items allowed to be kept and sold: all hard cheeses present and prosciutto (cured). These items have a lower water activity and therefore do not pose the same spoilage risk as the above items to be discarded. 

Facility’s hours of operation are 10a-7p. Discussed keeping a temperature log attached to cooler for staff to check periodically and document temperature in order to have records of ensuring temperatures are maintained and/or identify potential cooler failure and remove food from equipment in timely manner to minimize waste.
